description.narrative: 1. Hizmet-Is Union, the most representative union in the general services sector, established a platform aiming to support domestic workers' transition to registered work and enable them to enjoy union rights and be protected by the labour law, thus strengthening their representation. To further strengthen the voice and representation of domestic workers, Hizmet-s Union held a meeting on domestic work with the Board of Presidents, including representation of domestic workers (23 Sept. 2023). The President of HAKIS Confederation expressed commitment to achieve decent work for domestic workers. 2. Hizmet-Is Union conducted a petition campaign calling for decent work and formal employment for domestic workers in line with C189 (June 2023). The campaign was conducted at the HAKIS Confederation’s general assembly, to which Hizmet-Is Union is affiliated, in the presence of the President of Türkiye and the Minister of Labour and social security. The signatures serve as evidence of willingness and necessity for legal, social and economic demands for domestic workers. 3. The Directorate General of Labour established an inter-ministerial working group to assess and improve the working conditions of domestic workers. The Working Group’s terms of reference were approved by the DG of Labour. The Working Group’s first meeting was on the 14th of September, 2023, during which it adopted a strategy plan based on the ILO’s “Road to decent work for domestic workers”. The Working Group identified two priority areas for its first year: 1) improving data and 2) increasing formalization among domestic workers. These priorities will be implemented by subgroups that include social partners, including domestic workers’ unions. 4. Ankara Metropolitan Municipality raised awareness on domestic work through informative actions, including a poster campaign (2023) and workshop on OSH for domestic workers (2022). With support from SIDA, the ILO: 1.Kept domestic work on the agenda through an "Awareness-Raising Campaign for Decent Work for Domestic Workers", including an online meeting on “Access to Decent Work and Work Conditions for Domestic Workers” with Public Employment Agencies (April 2022), and a Conference on “Decent Work for Domestic Workers” (June 2022), consisting of a panel discussion on domestic workers’ rights and interviews of domestic workers by personalities of the art world to convey the message, “let’s pay dues to domestic workers”. These events included representatives from public agencies, workers’ organizations, civil society organizations and academia, and led to the union initiatives. 2.Prepared and disseminated advocacy and communication materials (poster on C189, infographics, e-cards, billboards, brochures and videos) as inputs to the union campaigns, and collaborated with the Actors' Union to produce celebrity videos on the working conditions of domestic workers. 3.Organized a Conference on “Decent Work for Domestic workers: Where we stand & what are the next steps?” (June 2023), which helped create a common understanding among public officials and trade unions on policy challenges, data gaps, and solutions to achieve decent work for domestic workers. During the Conference, the ILO presented its Road to decent work for domestic workers, on the basis of which participants decided to create the inter-ministerial working group. 4.Drafted terms of reference and a proposed strategy to the Working Group based on the ILO’s Roadmap "Road to decent work for domestic workers"; organized and moderated the Working Group’s first meeting; provided technical inputs; and will coordinate the subgroups for each priority area. 5.Provided technical support to the workshop on OSH for domestic workers and prepared the billboard message and listing solutions to ensure decent work for domestic workers, which were displayed on 25 screens across Ankara (2022)

description.narrative:
The programme « Transition to Formality (KIGEP) », since 2019, has been carried out in cooperation with the Social Security Institution (SSI), the Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MoLSS). Provincial branches of SSI have been strengthened to promote the workers’ transition from informal to formal employment in 16 provinces.
Under the ongoing collaboration among the ILO, Turkish Confederation of Tradesmen and Craftsmen (TESK) and its affiliated Chambers of Tradesmen and Craftsmen (ESOB) and the municipalities, technical support is being provided to strengthen the national governance institutions to assist Türkiye in implementing inclusive development strategies. Information Centres at local unions of tradesmen and craftsmen are established to provide improved services to informal businesses and their workers to provide information on public employment services and facilitate their transition to formality. Cooperative statistics were incorporated in the Official Statistics Program of Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat) and the new cooperative information system (KOOPBIS) of the Ministry of Trade was prepared in 2023, with an aim to facilitate the transition to formality of the cooperatives. With support from the German Development Bank (KfW) and the United States Department of State, Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration (USDOS PRM), the ILO continued to support SSI in the implementation of KIGEP, with a focus on its provincial branches, facilitating the opening of new local offices and providing technical equipment. The ILO also established a team of programme assistants placed in provincial directorates of SSI for smooth implementation and monitoring. As of June 2023, 8,653 workers (4,508 Syrians and 4,145 nationals) had been incentivized to be formally employed in 1,780 enterprises. The ILO, in collaboration with Chambers of Tradesmen and Craftsmen (ESOBs) and municipalities, established nine Information Centres (BILMER) with support contributions from KfW in different cities- Through these Centres, the ILO, together with relevant employers’ organizations, provides services to facilitate the formalization of enterprises and subsidies to cover registration fees. In 2023, the ILO supported nine BILMERS throughout Türkiye, benefitting 4,091 companies. The ILO’s initiative on advancing the Guidelines concerning Statistics of Cooperatives included Türkiye as a beneficiary country. Funded by the Ministry of Employment and Labour (MoEL) of the Republic of Korea; the initiative improved statistical guidelines in relation to cooperative development, enabling a gender-responsive monitoring system to assess progress towards the formalization of cooperatives. This includes refugee-inclusive women-run cooperatives.
